title_slide: Why the Same Advice Keeps Finding You

slides.heading: Why the Same Advice Keeps Finding You
bullet_points: You've heard it before — and nodded
Then closed the tab and changed nothing
This isn't a willpower problem
slides.speaker_note: Open with the recognition moment — most people in the room have lived this loop.

slides.heading: The $13B Industry's Real Problem
bullet_points: Same payload, infinite packaging
Sleep. Habits. Focus. Values. Presence.
The advice is mostly correct — delivery isn't the bottleneck
slides.speaker_note: Name the industry honestly before critiquing it — establishes credibility before the turn.

slides.heading: Advice Hits Differently Because You Changed
bullet_points: Same sentence, different life stage — completely different landing
Not a better author. More lived experience.
Advice needs soil. Soil is built from real experience, not reading.
slides.speaker_note: Use the 'protect your time' career example here — it's the most relatable concrete case.

slides.heading: Consumption as a Substitute for Discomfort
bullet_points: Learning triggers the same dopamine loop as actual progress
Finishing a book about discipline feels like being disciplined
The real work happens in private, with no audience and no reward
slides.speaker_note: This is the uncomfortable slide — say it directly, don't soften it.

slides.heading: What Actually Makes Advice Stick
bullet_points: Proximity to genuine cost — not manufactured urgency
When you've tried something and lived with the consequence
Advice that arrives close to experience has somewhere to anchor
slides.speaker_note: The mechanism is proximity, not volume — this is the core reframe of the whole piece.

slides.heading: You Cannot Skip the Sequence
bullet_points: Reading about grief does not prepare you for grief
Understanding is not immunity
Some things can only be lived through — and that's liberating, not defeatist
slides.speaker_note: Frame this as relief, not defeat — you can stop trying to learn your way out of things.

slides.heading: The Shift Worth Making
bullet_points: Treat advice as a pointer, not a shortcut
Ask: what am I actually ready to apply right now?
Stop optimizing for more learning — stay close to real experience
slides.speaker_note: End with the actionable reframe — this is what the audience walks away with.
